## Context / Problem

Nine real scanner integration tests skip when binaries are absent at `tests/unit/test_code_review_conflict_markers.py:97-158`, `test_code_review_public_exposure.py:109-151`, and `test_code_review_ws5.py:347-399`. Verified installs neither scanner although `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:43-71` makes them runtime prerequisites. The review-bot is deployed on Linux/arm64 Graviton while Verified runs on Linux/amd64, so their scanner pins must be platform-aware.

## Approach

Create one checked-in scanner lock manifest with separate `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` entries. Each entry records a Gitleaks version, its exact per-platform release URL, and SHA-256; the pinned checksum is taken from that release’s published `*_checksums.txt` asset at lock-update time. Each platform also references a fully resolved Semgrep requirements lock containing the same top-level Semgrep version and all platform-resolved distribution hashes. Provision Semgrep with `pip install --require-hashes`; do not represent this multi-wheel install as one fictional artifact hash.

Add one provisioning helper as the sole installation owner. It selects the manifest entry from Docker’s target OS/architecture or the CI runner’s actual OS/architecture, rejects an unsupported platform before installation, verifies the Gitleaks digest before extraction, and installs Semgrep only from the selected hash lock. The Graviton review-bot Docker build consumes `linux/arm64`; the Linux x64 reusable Verified lane consumes `linux/amd64`. Tests cover both selections rather than asserting that those different consumers share one binary artifact.

This deliberately supersedes dynamic-Gitleaks/latest and unpinned-Semgrep behavior. Stable per-release assets plus published checksums make reproducible, verified pins preferable; `docs/security.md` is generated, so the scanner-lock documentation is authored in `scripts/gen_config_reference.py`'s curated security narrative and then regenerated with `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`. The regenerated `docs/security.md` identifies the manifest, the checksum source, platform-lock update procedure, and the recovery action for a withdrawn asset (move both platform entries to an available verified release). Include a concrete worked example: bump Gitleaks by reading the release `*_checksums.txt`, updating each platform URL/SHA pair, regenerating Semgrep requirement locks with `pip --require-hashes`, running the installer validation target, and regenerating `docs/security.md`.

Add an explicit native-binary Make target that fails before its focused contracts for an unsupported platform, missing scanner, wrong Gitleaks version/digest, or missing/bad Semgrep requirement hash. It runs the nine real integration contracts only when a supported platform entry is provisioned. The existing skip-with-reason behavior remains for default local tests and unsupported developer platforms. Invoke the target from a reusable parallel workflow used by mirror CI and exact-patchset Gerrit verification, including the job in `vote.needs`.

Do not build Docker, install OpenGrep, or add this target to normal `make lint`/default local tests.

## Scope

- platform-aware scanner manifest, two Semgrep hash locks, and review-bot Dockerfile
- shared provisioning helper and explicit Make target
- scanner integration tests
- reusable mirror/Gerrit workflow and Verified parity guard
- `docs/security.md` scanner-lock ownership, update, checksum, and recovery procedure

## Testing

First prove the generated-document assumption: add a generator-level docs oracle that fails until `render_security()` emits the scanner-lock section, then prove the committed-doc drift check fails when the generator output changes without regenerating and passes after `python scripts/gen_config_reference.py`. Exercise manifest selection for Linux/amd64 and Linux/arm64, unsupported-platform rejection, missing Gitleaks, a bad Gitleaks SHA-256, a missing or bad Semgrep requirement hash, and wrong scanner versions. Prove valid selected locks pass the real Semgrep and Gitleaks contracts, that unsupported local platforms retain the skip-with-reason path, and that workflow wiring plus `vote.needs` parity hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The manifest has independent `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` scanner entries, each with an exact Gitleaks URL and SHA-256 sourced from the matching release `*_checksums.txt` asset.
- [ ] The review-bot Docker build selects and validates the `linux/arm64` entry; the reusable Linux x64 CI lane selects and validates the `linux/amd64` entry.
- [ ] Every platform entry points to a fully resolved Semgrep requirements lock with an identical top-level Semgrep version and all required distribution hashes; the installer uses `pip --require-hashes`.
- [ ] The installer rejects an unsupported platform, missing scanner, wrong Gitleaks version/digest, and invalid Semgrep hash before it runs the focused contracts.
- [ ] Valid selected scanner locks allow the explicit native-binary target to pass all nine real Semgrep/Gitleaks integration contracts.
- [ ] Default local tests on unsupported platforms preserve the existing skip-with-reason behavior and do not provision scanners.
- [ ] `scripts/gen_config_reference.py` owns a curated scanner-lock security narrative; regenerated `docs/security.md` names the manifest as the update authority, the checksum source, a concrete per-platform bump example, and the withdrawn-asset recovery procedure.
- [ ] One parallel reusable lane serves mirror CI and exact Gerrit patchsets and is required by the Verified vote.
- [ ] A generator-level docs oracle proves the scanner-lock section appears in regenerated `docs/security.md`, and the existing drift check proves committed `docs/security.md` fails when generator content changes without regeneration and passes after regeneration.
- [ ] OpenGrep, Docker-image builds, normal `make lint`, and default local tests remain outside scope.
- [ ] The lane's expected cold-run cost is documented as approximately 1.5-3 runner-minutes without extending the existing 22-23 minute critical path when capacity is available.
